title: What If a Country Switched Sides of the Road Overnight?

scenes.text: What if a whole country switched sides of the road overnight? Sweden did, at exactly 5 a.m.
In 1955, 83 percent of Swedish voters said no to the change. Parliament approved it anyway in 1963.
Early on 3 September 1967, every vehicle stopped at 4:50 a.m. and switched sides at 5:00.
About 350,000 road signs were removed or replaced, about 20,000 of them in Stockholm.
That Sunday saw 157 minor accidents, 32 with injuries, and the next Monday only 125, with no deaths.
Insurance claims dropped 40 percent, but the gains faded. By 1969, accident rates were back to where they began.
